 NPS KYC Rules For NRI And OCI Seafarers Amended: What Subscribers Need To Know
 The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) has eased NPS KYC documentation requirements for NRI and OCI seafarers, who faced issues opening an NPS account due to stringent KYC requirements. The regulator amended the rules to make it easier for the seafarers to enrol under NPS
 Versha Jain Updated on: 17 November 2026 12:15 pm Updated on: 17 November 2026 12:15 pm SUBSCRIBE 
 PFRDA eases NPS KYC rules for NRI, OCI seafarers Photo: AI PFRDA eases NPS KYC rules for NRI, OCI seafarers Photo: AI Summary of this article
 PFRDA eases NPS KYC rules for NRI and OCI seafarers, effective November 13, 2026.
 An employment contract or recent CDC is accepted as address proof.
 Onboard seafarers may use their employer or Indian address as address proof.
 The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) issued a circular revising the know your customer (KYC) requirements for Non-Resident Indian (NRI) and Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) subscribers with a seafarer work profile. The circular dated November 13, 2026, addresses the onboarding issues maritime personnel face when opening a National Pension System (NPS) Tier I account.
 Under the existing rules based on the circular dated December 2, 2025, and the Master circular on anti-money laundering and combating the financing of terrorism (KYC/AML/CFT) dated September 25, the NRI and OCI subscribers need to submit the Customer Due Diligence (CDD) and Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) along with the specific documentation confirming their proof of Identity (PoI) and proof of address (PoA).

So, to make the NPS account opening process easier for them (NRI and OCI applicants holding a seafarer profile), PFRDA amended the standard KYC documentation for them.
 PFRDA inserted point (iv) into the “Note” section of Para 8.3 (a) under the circular dated December 2, 2025, to effect this amendment. Now, all regulatory entities (REs) must accept either a valid PoA for onboarding NRI seafarers into an NPS account. These two documents are:
 A valid employment contract executed with the employer or shipping company, when a seafarer is proceeding on a fresh contract.
 A Continuous Discharge Certificate (CDC), provided that the disembarkation stamp or official record inside is not more than six months old.

 BY Versha Jain 
 KYC Rules For Currently Onboarded NRI Seafarers 
 NRI seafarers who are currently on board a vessel and want to register for NPS, the recent changes offer them flexibility regarding address documentation. Such onboard subscribers can provide either the overseas address of their employer or the Indian address of the subscriber.
 The changes in the KYC rules have been made effective from November 13, 2026. All other terms and conditions and requirements under the December 2, 2025 circular and the September 25, 2026 master circular remain unchanged.
 The change in KYC requirements is expected to make onboarding of the NRI and OCI seafarers easier. The directive has been issued to all points of presence (PoPs) , Central Recordkeeping Agencies (CRAs), NPS Trust, and industry stakeholders for incorporating the changes.
